entries.title: 📱 The algorithm wants {client}
entries.text:
[i]“Our completion-rate models love {client}'s face. Eight episodes, drop them all at once, global day-and-date. The offer expires when the dashboard changes its mind.”[/i]

A streamer's deal memo: excellent money, brutal pace, and fame measured in weekends instead of years.

choices.label: Sign the algorithm series

effects.text: {client} signs with the streamer — the dashboard is pleased.

choices.outcome: The deal closes in forty-eight hours, which in this business means somebody's model was very sure. By the drop weekend, {client} is everywhere — for a weekend.

choices.label: Pass — stay scarce, stay cinema

effects.text: {client} passes on the streamer. The algorithm shrugs and casts someone similar.

choices.outcome: The dashboard finds another face within the hour. Scarcity still works — but the feed forgets faster than the town ever did.

entries.title: 📱 The algorithm wants more
entries.text: The show 'over-performed against model' — and the streamer wants season two in front of cameras within weeks, while the completion curves are hot. The offer is generous. The calendar is not.

choices.label: Deliver season two back-to-back

effects.text: Season two, back-to-back: the money is great and {client} is running on fumes.

choices.outcome: The curves stay hot, the bonus lands, and {client} learns what 'day-and-date' does to a human being.

choices.label: Make the algorithm wait

effects.text: You negotiate breathing room before season two. The dashboard sulks; {client} sleeps.

choices.outcome: You get the gap year. The streamer's models call it 'audience risk'. Your client calls it a life.

effects_fail.text: The streamer will not wait — the slot goes cold and so does the show's heat.

choices.outcome_fail: The streamer reshuffles the slate and the show slides down the carousel. The feed has already half forgotten it.

entries.title: 🫥 The digital double: {client}
entries.text:
[i]“Full volumetric scan, perpetual license, 'future formats included'. The number at the bottom has a lot of zeroes.”[/i]

The studio wants {client}'s likeness — every angle, every expression, forever. The lawyers call it standard now. Nothing about it feels standard.

choices.label: Sell the scan — take the zeroes

effects.text: {client}'s likeness is licensed — perpetually. The zeroes were persuasive.

choices.outcome: The scan takes an afternoon. {client} watches the rig circle and says, quietly: “So that's what I'll be doing after I'm dead.”

choices.label: Negotiate hard limits — usage, approval, sunset clause

effects.text: A likeness deal with teeth: limits, approvals, sunset. {client} sleeps fine.

choices.outcome: Half the zeroes, all the control. The studio's lawyers respect nothing as much as a contract they couldn't hollow out.

effects_fail.text: The likeness negotiation collapses — the studio calls your limits 'legacy thinking'.

choices.outcome_fail: They pull the offer rather than accept a sunset clause. Somewhere on the lot, a model of {client} stays unbuilt — for now.

choices.label: Refuse on principle

effects.text: {client}'s face stays {client}'s. The studio files the refusal under 'difficult'.

choices.outcome: “A face is a career,” you tell the lawyers, “and careers are not perpetual licenses.” {client} hears about the refusal and sends a very old bottle of wine.

entries.title: 🫥 The double appears
entries.text: It surfaces in a trailer nobody sent over: {client}'s face — younger, smoother, saying lines {client} never said. The license covers it. That is precisely the problem.

choices.label: Lawyers, loudly

effects.text: You fight the double's cameo — expensive, but {client} sees you swing.

choices.outcome: You lose on the letter of the contract and win on the noise: the studio quietly shelves the double's next three appearances.

choices.label: Let it slide — the license is the license

effects.text: That new trailer? {client} never set foot on that stage — and people are starting to say so.
The double works and {client} watches. The internet notices the difference.

choices.outcome: Contractually spotless, humanly corrosive. {client} stops watching trailers altogether.
